one_line: The APOE-R136S (Christchurch) mutation protects against APOE4-driven Tau pathology, neurodegeneration, and neuroinflammation in a gene dose-dependent manner.
summary: This study investigates whether the rare APOE-R136S (Christchurch) mutation, known to protect against early-onset Alzheimer's disease, also mitigates the detrimental effects of the APOE4 allele in late-onset AD models. Using human APOE4 knock-in tauopathy mice and human iPSC-derived neurons, the researchers discovered that the homozygous R136S mutation fully rescued APOE4-driven Tau pathology, neurodegeneration, and neuroinflammation. The heterozygous mutation provided partial protection against neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation but did not reduce Tau pathology. Mechanistically, the R136S mutation impaired HSPG-mediated neuronal Tau uptake, blunting p-Tau accumulation. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed that the mutation dose-dependently enriched disease-protective glial populations while diminishing disease-associated astrocytes, microglia, and oligodendrocytes.

key_claims.claim: The homozygous APOE-R136S mutation rescues APOE4-driven Tau pathology, neurodegeneration, and neuroinflammation.
key_claims.evidence: PS19-E4-S/S mice showed significantly reduced AT8+ p-Tau coverage compared to PS19-E4 mice, full rescue of hippocampal and lateral ventricle volumes, and significant reductions in GFAP+, S100β+, Iba1+, and CD68+ glial cells.

key_claims.claim: The heterozygous APOE-R136S mutation provides partial protection against neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation but not Tau pathology.
key_claims.evidence: PS19-E4-R/S mice maintained ~90% type 3/4 p-Tau staining but still exhibited partially rescued hippocampal atrophy and significant, dose-dependent reductions in astrocytosis and microgliosis compared to PS19-E4.

key_claims.claim: The R136S mutation protects against p-Tau accumulation by reducing Tau uptake via the HSPG pathway.
key_claims.evidence: E4-S/S human neurons exhibited a ~50% reduction in Tau-488 uptake compared to E4 neurons. Heparin treatment (blocking HSPGs) reduced p-Tau levels in E4 neurons by ~25% but did not significantly alter them in E4-S/S neurons.

key_claims.claim: The APOE4-R136S mutation shifts cell transcriptomics by increasing disease-protective glia and diminishing disease-associated cells.
key_claims.evidence: snRNA-seq on 175,080 nuclei demonstrated that E4-S/S enriched homeostatic astrocytes (cluster 3) and microglia (clusters 2, 11) while essentially eliminating disease-associated oligodendrocytes (cluster 9), astrocytes (clusters 5, 7), and microglia (cluster 8).

methods.design: In vivo study using human APOE4 knock-in tauopathy mice (PS19-E) combined with CRISPR-edited human iPSC-derived neuron models.
methods.n: snRNA-seq: 175,080 nuclei from 15 mice; histology/volumetric analyses used n=20-31 mice per group.
methods.population: PS19-E4, PS19-E3, PS19-E4-S/S, and PS19-E4-R/S mice (C57BL/6 background) and isogenic hiPSC lines derived from an APOE4/4 AD patient.
methods.duration: Mice evaluated at 6 and 10 months of age.

limitations: The models lack extensive Aβ pathology, meaning the study does not address whether APOE-R136S protects against Aβ-mediated inflammatory and neurodegenerative effects.

The study evaluates the R136S mutation entirely within the APOE4 allele background, whereas the original protected patient had the mutation on an APOE3 background; protection in an APOE3 context remains to be studied.
